quizzes.label: Math Precalculus PC.1B

reflect across the y-axis, then translate up 2 units

Base angles in a triangle are always right angles
questions.explanation: Patterns can be used to make conjectures, but a proof is needed to confirm the conjecture in general.

quizzes.description: G.13C: determine probabilities for events with and without replacement and recognize when events are independent Sources: https://tea.texas.gov/academics/instructional-materials/review-and-adoption-process/breakout-documents/geometry.pdf and https://tea.texas.gov/about-tea/laws-and-rules/texas-administrative-code/19-tac-chapter-111

questions.prompt: A bag has 3 red marbles and 2 blue marbles. If a marble is drawn, replaced, and then another is drawn, what is the probability of drawing two red marbles?
questions.explanation: With replacement, the draws are independent, so multiply the same single-draw probability twice.

questions.prompt: A bag has 4 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. If two marbles are drawn without replacement, what is the probability of drawing two red marbles?
questions.explanation: Without replacement, the probabilities change after the first draw, so the events are not independent.

questions.prompt: Which situation describes independent events?
options: Selecting a card and not replacing it before choosing another
Choosing two students from a class without replacement
Selecting a card, replacing it, and then selecting another card
Taking marbles from a bag without replacement
questions.explanation: Events are independent when the outcome of one does not change the probability of the other.

quizzes.description: G.13E: determine whether events are independent and justify the conclusion Sources: https://tea.texas.gov/academics/instructional-materials/review-and-adoption-process/breakout-documents/geometry.pdf and https://tea.texas.gov/about-tea/laws-and-rules/texas-administrative-code/19-tac-chapter-111

questions.prompt: Event A has probability 1/2, event B has probability 1/3, and P(A and B) = 1/6. Are the events independent?
options: Yes, because independent events always have equal probabilities
No, because one event has probability 1/2
No, because the probabilities are different
Yes, because P(A and B) = P(A)P(B)
questions.explanation: Events are independent when the probability of both occurring equals the product of their individual probabilities.

questions.prompt: Which pair of events is independent?
options: Drawing two marbles from a bag without replacement
Drawing two cards from a deck without replacement
Choosing two students from a class without replacement
Flipping a coin and rolling a number cube
questions.explanation: Separate random processes such as a coin flip and a die roll do not affect each other.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes events that are not independent?
options: The outcome of the first event changes the probability of the second event
Both events must happen at the same time
The first and second events always have the same probability
questions.explanation: Dependent events are not independent because one result changes the probability of the next result.

questions.explanation: The coefficient of x in slope-intercept form is the slope.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares a figure and its dilation on a coordinate plane?
options: Angle measures change but side lengths stay the same
Both angle measures and side lengths stay exactly the same

A dilation always turns the figure upside down
questions.explanation: Dilations preserve angle measure and change lengths proportionally.

questions.explanation: The rate of change gives the slope and the value at x = 0 gives the y-intercept.

questions.prompt: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with length 4, width 3, and height 5?
questions.explanation: Volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height.

questions.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangular base area of 24 square units and a prism length of 5 units. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume of any prism is base area times prism length.

questions.prompt: A rectangular pyramid has a base area of 54 square units and height 12 units. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume of a pyramid is one-third the product of base area and height.

questions.explanation: A pyramid's volume is one-third of the matching prism with the same base area and height.

questions.explanation: Total surface area is the sum of all face areas in the net.

questions.explanation: Lateral surface area includes only the side faces, not the bases.

quizzes.label: Math Grade 7 7.12B
quizzes.description: 7.12B: use data from a random sample to make inferences about a population Sources: https://tea.texas.gov/student-assessment/staar/staar-7-math-assessed-curriculum.pdf and https://tea.texas.gov/student-assessment/staar/staar-7-math-blueprint.pdf

questions.prompt: In a random sample of 20 students, 6 said they bring lunch from home. About how many in a population of 100 students would you expect to bring lunch from home?
questions.explanation: Use the sample proportion to make an inference about the population.

questions.prompt: A random sample of 30 voters found that 10 support a proposal. Which is a reasonable inference about the population?
options: About 33% of the population may support the proposal
The sample proves every person supports it
No one in the population supports it
Exactly 10 people in the population support it
questions.explanation: Random samples can suggest what may be true in the whole population, but they do not guarantee exact results.

questions.prompt: In a random sample of 40 students, 14 said they bring lunch from home. About how many in a population of 200 students would you expect to bring lunch from home?
questions.explanation: Use the sample proportion to make an inference about the population.

questions.explanation: Random samples can suggest what may be true in the whole population, but they do not guarantee exact results.

quizzes.description: 7.12C: compare two populations based on data in random samples from these populations, including informal comparative inferences about differences between the two populations Sources: https://tea.texas.gov/student-assessment/staar/staar-7-math-assessed-curriculum.pdf and https://tea.texas.gov/student-assessment/staar/staar-7-math-blueprint.pdf

questions.prompt: A random sample from Town A has median travel time 12 minutes. A random sample from Town B has median travel time 16 minutes. Which population likely has the higher center?

questions.explanation: Comparing sample percentages can support informal inferences about differences between populations.

questions.explanation: Sales tax is found by multiplying the purchase amount by the tax rate.
